messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

For raw report histories, we need to process the events as per specified rule: "first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order." The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions. After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.

We must return five integers through submit_answer:
- stock_at_target: the stock after processing historical events up to target_time inclusive (i.e., after applying all eligible events visible as of knowledge_cutoff and with event_time <= target_time).
- total historical_lost: total lost demand (unmet demand) through target_time using visible revisions (i.e., sum of (demand_quantity - quantity_fulfilled) for applicable historical events, only for events meeting the process up to target_time). Note that a stockout is defined as strictly positive unmet demand. So any demand that is partially or fully unmet yields lost quantity; we add that to historical_lost. But a demand that is fully met (stock >= demand) yields no lost. Also note that "lost" means unmet demand due to insufficient inventory at time of demand; they do not backorder, they are lost. So our lost count is sum of unmet pieces.
- stock_at_horizon: after processing historical events and then processing future_schedule and any events up to horizon_time inclusive; we need the stock after processing all events up to horizon_time inclusive. Horizon_time is 130. The future_schedule includes events up to time 129 (event_id F-11). So horizon_time is after all future events. So stock_at_horizon = final stock after applying the future schedule events (i.e., after processing both historical and future events). It includes all events up to horizon_time inclusive (including future events up to 129). So we need final stock after processing future events; horizon_time > last event time, so final stock is after all future events.

- future_lost: total lost demand for the scenario ONLY, i.e., from future_schedule events only (so we ignore any lost that occurs from historical events). We need to sum unmet quantities for each future demand event (including those after previous future receipts may have replenished stock). The future schedule includes demands at times: 103, 106, 109, 114, 116, 129? Actually check: F-00 demand 8 at 103; F-02 demand 12 at 106; F-04 demand 6 at 109; F-06 demand 4 at 114; F-07 demand 6 at 116; F-11 demand 6 at 129. So we need to compute unmet demand for each of these, after processing receipts and prior demands in order (including the receipts at times: 105, 107, 112, 117, 118, 127). There may be stockouts leading to lost, we sum these.

- first_future_stockout_time: earliest future scenario event time (i.e., among future_schedule events) with unmet demand > 0, i.e., first time where demand was not fully met (i.e., stock at start of that demand < quantity). If all future demands are fully satisfied (i.e., no unmet demand), return -1.
